# amendsheet

Read, edit and create `.xlsx` files in Node or the browser. Every part you do not
touch is written back byte for byte, so charts, pivot tables, drawings and macros
survive a read and a save. Changing one cell never quietly discards the rest of
the workbook. One runtime dependency (`fflate`), no transitive tree.

This file is the complete API for an LLM writing code against the library. Every
example below typechecks against the real exports. Prefer it over guessing.

## Why reach for this

- **It does not lose data.** Parts the library does not interpret are preserved
  exactly. Editing a cell in a chart-heavy workbook keeps the charts.
- **It fails loudly, never silently.** A value a cell cannot hold, a bad
  reference or an unsupported edit throws a located `XlsxError` — it does not
  guess and write something wrong. You can react to the error and move on.
- **Types guide you.** Options are discriminated unions, so the shape you need is
  visible and an invalid one will not compile.

## Install

```
npm install amendsheet
```

No Node-only APIs in the core, so it runs in the browser too. Read from a
`Uint8Array` and write to one; do the file or network IO yourself at the edges.

## The core loop: read, edit, write

```ts
const workbook = readWorkbook(bytes) // bytes: Uint8Array of an .xlsx
const sheet = workbook.sheet('Summary') ?? workbook.sheets[0]

sheet?.set('B2', 42)

const out = workbook.toBytes() // synchronous, returns Uint8Array
await writeFile('out.xlsx', out)
```

Create a new workbook instead of reading one:

```ts
const workbook = createWorkbook('Report') // optional sheet name, default 'Sheet1'
const sheet = workbook.addSheet('Data') // add more sheets
sheet.set('A1', 'hello')
const out = workbook.toBytes()
```

`readWorkbook` and `createWorkbook` are the only two entry points. Both return a
`Workbook`; everything else hangs off it or off a `Worksheet`.

## Reading cells

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

for (const cell of sheet?.cells() ?? []) {
  // cell.reference ('B2'), cell.value, cell.formula, cell.numberFormat,
  // cell.font, cell.fill, cell.border, cell.alignment, cell.comment, cell.hyperlink
  if (cell.value.kind === 'number') cell.value.value
  if (cell.value.kind === 'text') cell.value.value
  if (cell.value.kind === 'date') cell.value.value // a Date
}

const one = sheet?.cell('B2') // undefined if the sheet stores nothing there
```

`cell.value` is a discriminated union on `kind`: `'number'`, `'text'`, `'date'`,
`'boolean'`, `'error'`, `'empty'`. A cell that holds only formatting, or that a
comment sits on with no value of its own, still appears, as `kind: 'empty'`.

## Writing cells

```ts
const sheet = createWorkbook().sheets[0]

sheet?.set('A1', 42)
sheet?.set('A2', 'text')
sheet?.set('A3', true)
sheet?.set('A4', new Date('2024-01-01')) // gains a date format if it has none
sheet?.set('A5', { formula: 'SUM(A1:A4)' })
sheet?.set('A6', null) // clears the value, keeps the formatting
sheet?.set('A7', 1234.5, { numberFormat: '"$"#,##0.00' })
```

`set(reference, value, options?)` takes a `number | string | boolean | Date |
{ formula } | null`. A missing cell, its row, and the sheet dimension are all
created to cover it. A replaced cell keeps its style. `set` throws
`unwritable-value` for a value a chosen format cannot hold, and records nothing
when it does, so the rest of a batch still writes.

## Formatting

Formatting composes through the same `options`, and each part merges onto what the
cell already has:

```ts
const sheet = createWorkbook().sheets[0]

sheet?.set('A1', 1234.5, {
  numberFormat: '"$"#,##0.00',
  font: { bold: true, italic: false, size: 12, color: 'FF0000', name: 'Calibri' },
  fill: { type: 'solid', color: 'FFFF00' },
  border: { all: { style: 'thin' }, bottom: { style: 'medium', color: '000000' } },
  alignment: { horizontal: 'center', vertical: 'center', wrapText: true },
  protection: { locked: false },
})

// format() changes only formatting, so a formula cell keeps its expression.
sheet?.format('B2', { font: { bold: true } })
```

- **font**: `bold`, `italic`, `size`, `color`, `name`, `strike`, `underline`
  (`true | 'double' | 'singleAccounting' | 'doubleAccounting'`), `verticalAlign`
  (`'superscript' | 'subscript'`). Merges onto the current font.
- **fill**: `{ type: 'solid', color }` or `{ type: 'pattern', pattern, color,
  background }` (`pattern` is an ECMA-376 name like `'lightGrid'`).
- **border**: sides by name (`top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`), `all` for every side,
  or `diagonal` (`{ style, color?, up?, down? }`). `style` is a name like `'thin'`,
  `'medium'`, `'dashed'`.
- **alignment**: `horizontal`, `vertical`, `wrapText`, `textRotation` (0–180, or
  255 to stack), `indent`.
- **protection**: `locked`, `hidden` — bite once the sheet is protected.
- A **colour** is an `'RRGGBB'` or `'AARRGGBB'` hex, a theme `{ theme, tint }`, or
  an indexed `{ indexed }`. `workbook.resolveColor(color)` turns a reference into
  the hex it shows as.

## Structure: merges, rows, columns

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.merge('A1:B2') // top-left value shows; joins existing merges
sheet?.unmerge('A1:B2') // removes exactly that merge; a range it lacks is ignored
sheet?.mergedRanges // readonly string[], e.g. ['A1:B2']

sheet?.setRowHeight(1, 30) // points
sheet?.setColumnWidth('A', 18) // Excel width units
sheet?.rowHeight(1) // number | undefined
sheet?.columnWidth('A') // number | undefined

sheet?.hideRow(2)
sheet?.hideColumn('C')
sheet?.isRowHidden(2) // boolean
sheet?.isColumnHidden('C') // boolean

sheet?.groupRows(2, 5) // outline level 1..7 (default 1)
sheet?.groupColumns('B', 'D')
sheet?.rowGroupLevel(2) // 0 when not grouped
sheet?.columnGroupLevel('B')

sheet?.insertRows(3, 2) // 2 blank rows before row 3; references shift
sheet?.insertColumns('C') // 1 blank column before C
sheet?.deleteRows(3, 2)
sheet?.deleteColumns('C')
```

Insert/delete shift every reference that points into the moved lines — formulas
across the whole workbook, merges, filters, conditional formats, defined names.
They also move a table's own range and a comment's cell (its box in the legacy
drawing moves too, and a note whose cell a deletion removes is dropped). A table
below or beside the edit shifts with it, and a deletion that clips it shrinks it,
dropping the column entries it cut out. A column inserted inside a table is
refused with `unsupported-edit` (no new column entry is authored yet), as is a
deletion that would take every column of a table or its header row. An edit on a
sheet carrying a drawing, pivot table or chart is still refused. A delete that
would strand a `#REF!` a merge or shared formula cannot survive is refused too.

## Data validation

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.validate('A1:A10', { list: ['Low', 'Medium', 'High'] }) // inline dropdown
sheet?.validate('B1', { listRange: 'Sheet1!$A$1:$A$3' }) // dropdown from a range
sheet?.validate('C1', { whole: { between: [1, 100] } })
sheet?.validate('D1', { decimal: { greaterThan: 0 } })
sheet?.validate('E1', { textLength: { lessThanOrEqual: 40 } })
sheet?.validate('F1', { date: { between: [new Date('2024-01-01'), new Date('2024-12-31')] } })
sheet?.validate('G1', { custom: 'ISNUMBER(G1)' }, )

sheet?.validations // readonly [{ range, rule }] — reads the file plus pending
sheet?.clearValidations() // removes all; a validate() after still applies
```

A comparison (`whole`/`decimal`/`textLength`/`date`) is keyed by operator:
`between`/`notBetween` (a `[min, max]` pair), or `equal`/`notEqual`/`greaterThan`/
`lessThan`/`greaterThanOrEqual`/`lessThanOrEqual` (a single bound). `date` bounds
are `Date`s. Add `allowBlank: false` to any rule to forbid an empty cell.

## Conditional formatting

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.conditionalFormat('A1:A20', { colorScale: { min: 'F8696B', mid: 'FFEB84', max: '63BE7B' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('B1:B20', { dataBar: { color: '638EC6' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('C1:C20', { cellIs: { when: { greaterThan: 100 }, fill: 'FFC7CE' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('D1:D20', { expression: { formula: '$D1>AVERAGE($D:$D)', fill: 'FFFF00' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('E1:E20', { duplicates: { fill: 'FFC7CE' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('F1:F20', { unique: { fill: 'C6EFCE' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('G1:G20', { top: { count: 5, fill: 'C6EFCE' } })
sheet?.conditionalFormat('H1:H20', { bottom: { count: 10, fill: 'FFC7CE', percent: true } })

sheet?.conditionalFormats // readonly [{ range, rule }]
sheet?.clearConditionalFormats() // removes all; a conditionalFormat() after still applies
```

A `colorScale` grades between two hex stops, or three with `mid`. The `cellIs`,
`expression`, `duplicates`, `unique`, `top` and `bottom` rules each fill matching
cells with a hex `fill`. `top`/`bottom` take a `count`, and `percent: true` reads
the count as a percentage.

## Comments and hyperlinks

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.comment('A1', 'A note that shows on hover.')
sheet?.removeComment('A1') // removes the note and its box; a cell without one is ignored
sheet?.cell('A1')?.comment // the text, when read back

sheet?.link('B2', { url: 'https://example.com', tooltip: 'Open' })
sheet?.link('B3', { location: 'Sheet2!A1' }) // a place in the workbook
sheet?.unlink('B2') // removes the link; a cell without one is ignored
sheet?.cell('B2')?.hyperlink // { url } or { location }
```

`comment` adds a note (and, on a sheet that already has notes, splices in without
disturbing the rich text already there); it refuses only a cell that already
carries one. `link` replaces any link on the cell.

## Sheet view

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.freeze('B2') // freezes row 1 and column A
sheet?.tabColor('FF0000')
sheet?.showGridlines(false)
sheet?.showHeadings(false)
sheet?.zoom(150)
sheet?.autoFilter('A1:D1')

// The matching reads — note the names, since the plain nouns are the setters:
sheet?.frozenAt // 'B2' | undefined
sheet?.tabColorHex // 'FFFF0000' | undefined
sheet?.gridlinesVisible // boolean
sheet?.headingsVisible // boolean
sheet?.zoomPercent // number | undefined
sheet?.autoFilterRange // 'A1:D1' | undefined
```

## Page setup for printing

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.setPageSetup({ orientation: 'landscape', scale: 90 }) // scale 10..400
sheet?.setPageMargins({ left: 1, right: 1 }) // inches; merges onto the rest
sheet?.pageSetup // { orientation?, scale? }
sheet?.pageMargins // { left?, right?, top?, bottom?, header?, footer? }
```

`setPageSetup` keeps any other `pageSetup` attribute the sheet has; `setPageMargins`
fills the other five from what the sheet had (or Excel's defaults), so a partial
edit still writes a complete element. Note the read/write split: `pageSetup` reads,
`setPageSetup` writes.

## Sheets and the workbook

```ts
const workbook = readWorkbook(bytes)

workbook.sheets // readonly Worksheet[]
workbook.sheet('Data') // by name, undefined if none
const added = workbook.addSheet('New')
added.rename('Renamed')
added.setState('hidden') // 'visible' | 'hidden' | 'veryHidden'; refuses the last visible sheet
added.state // reads it back, reflecting a pending setState
added.remove() // a workbook must keep at least one sheet

workbook.definedNames // ReadonlyMap<name, formula>
workbook.defineName('Tax', 'Sheet1!$B$1')
workbook.removeDefinedName('Tax') // a name it lacks is ignored

workbook.epoch // 1900 | 1904 — the date system
```

Document properties (`docProps/core.xml`):

```ts
const workbook = readWorkbook(bytes)

workbook.properties // { title?, subject?, creator?, keywords?, description?, lastModifiedBy?, created?, modified? }
workbook.setProperties({ title: 'Q3 Report', creator: 'Ada', created: new Date() })
```

`setProperties` merges — each field replaces the one the file had and leaves the
rest (including properties this does not model) untouched, creating the part when
the file has none. `created` and `modified` are `Date`s.

## Sheet protection

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]

sheet?.protect() // Excel's default: everything locked
sheet?.protect({ formatCells: true }) // permit specific actions
sheet?.unprotect()
sheet?.protection // the SheetProtection in force, or undefined
```

Cell `locked`/`hidden` flags only bite once the sheet is protected. Passwords are
not written.

## Errors

Every failure is an `XlsxError` with a `.code` and a message that names what
failed and where. Switch on the code; it is an open union, so keep a default.

```ts
import { XlsxError, readWorkbook } from 'amendsheet'

try {
  const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]
  sheet?.set('not a reference', 5) // throws
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof XlsxError) {
    error.code // 'bad-reference' | 'unwritable-value' | 'unsupported-edit' | ...
    error.message // located, human-readable
  }
}
```

`bad-reference` and `unwritable-value` mean the caller passed something wrong;
every other code means the file did. This split lets you tell a bug in your code
from a quirk of the input.

## Recipes

Turn a range into a banded, filterable table (the header row must have values, or
pass `columns`):

```ts
const workbook = createWorkbook('Report')
const sheet = workbook.sheets[0]
sheet?.set('A1', 'Name')
sheet?.set('B1', 'Total')
sheet?.set('A2', 'Ada')
sheet?.set('B2', 42)
sheet?.addTable('A1:B2', { name: 'People', style: 'TableStyleMedium2' })
sheet?.tables // readonly [{ name, range, columns }]
```

`addTable` sets the header cells to the column names — from `columns`, the header
cells already there, or `Column1`, `Column2`… It refuses a bad range, a duplicate
or empty column name, a table name the workbook uses, or an overlap.

Fill a fresh sheet from rows of data:

```ts
const workbook = createWorkbook('Report')
const sheet = workbook.sheets[0]
const rows = [['Name', 'Total'], ['Ada', 42], ['Grace', 37]]
rows.forEach((row, r) => {
  row.forEach((value, c) => {
    const reference = `${String.fromCharCode(65 + c)}${r + 1}`
    sheet?.set(reference, value, r === 0 ? { font: { bold: true } } : undefined)
  })
})
const out = workbook.toBytes()
```

Highlight the cells above a threshold, and freeze the header:

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]
sheet?.freeze('A2')
sheet?.conditionalFormat('B2:B100', { cellIs: { when: { greaterThan: 1000 }, fill: 'FFC7CE' } })
```

Add a dropdown and stamp the author-ish title cell:

```ts
const sheet = readWorkbook(bytes).sheets[0]
sheet?.validate('C2:C100', { list: ['Open', 'Closed'] })
sheet?.set('A1', 'Status Report', { font: { bold: true, size: 14 } })
```

## Gotchas

- **Read-accessor names.** Where a setter took the plain noun, the getter says
  what it returns: `tabColor(...)` sets, `tabColorHex` reads; `freeze(...)` /
  `frozenAt`; `zoom(...)` / `zoomPercent`; `autoFilter(...)` / `autoFilterRange`;
  `showGridlines(...)` / `gridlinesVisible`.
- **Immutable by default and synchronous.** Edits are recorded on the workbook and
  applied by `toBytes()`, which returns a `Uint8Array` — no promises, no streams.
- **`cells()` re-reads the sheet each call.** Iterate once; do not call it per
  cell.
- **The ZIP is rebuilt on write.** An untouched file comes back the same document
  but not the same bytes (compression and entry order are the writer's own); the
  parts and values are preserved, which is the guarantee that matters.
